newsitem.title: USA: A-10 jet crashes in Georgia - U.S. Air Force.
newsitem.headline: A-10 jet crashes in Georgia - U.S. Air Force.

text.p: An Air Force A-10 attack jet crashed at a practice weapons range in northern Georgia on Thursday but initial reports indicated the pilot ejected safely, the Air Force said.

Maj. Ed Worley, an Air Force spokesman at the Pentagon, said the plane was based at Moody Air Force Base near Valdosta, Georgia, and went down on Thursday afternoon at Townsend Range southwest of Savannah.
"The plane crashed," he said. "We have an unconfirmed report that the pilot ejected from the aircraft."

The incident occurred as rescue units continued to search the Colorado mountains for another Air Force A-10 that disappeared mysteriously on April 2 during a routine training mission that began in Arizona.
The training range in Georgia is about 60 miles east-northeast of Valdosta, Worley said.
